title: Learned synthetic CT enables physically tested lung-radiotherapy dose planning
summary: A UNet++ model converted cone-beam scans into synthetic CT images for lung-cancer radiotherapy planning. Plans based on 17 patients’ images were compared with planning-CT references and checked through actual phantom irradiation. Measured dose deviations were 2–7%, comparable to the reference-plan deviations in that experiment. This supports a bounded medical-physics feasibility result, not formal dosimetric equivalence, improved patient outcomes or demonstrated adaptive treatment delivery.
ai_technology: UNet++ with ResNet50 backbone for synthetic CT generation
organization: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; MedMind Technology; Tsinghua University

evidence.tested: Model development used 70 patients and image evaluation 15;17 additional patients supplied paired cone-beam/planning CT scans for offline planning comparisons. Generated-image plans underwent physical ArcCHECK and thermoluminescent-dose measurements on phantoms, with 2–7% dose deviations reported.
evidence.unknown: The clinical images and plan comparison were retrospective; phantom irradiation does not establish actual adaptive patient-treatment benefit. Nonsignificant dose differences do not prove equivalence. The tumor-volume gradient index differed, and some tumor-dose metrics had weaker agreement. The source’s percentage image-MAE improvement is inconsistent with its displayed means and is not reproduced here. Validation is limited to the studied scanner/workflow and geometry.
evidence.ai_role: UNet++ learns the image-to-image conversion needed to reduce cone-beam CT intensity errors before conventional dose calculation. The generated-image plans, rather than only image-quality scores, are tested against physical dose measurements.

source_review.scope: Exact primary XML front DOI/title/date; full patient/model Methods, generated-plan comparison and actual phantom/TLD measurement Results. Fresh Crossref publication-status metadata; PubMed/EPMC status access was limited.
